body: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了STAMP（基于序列树附件的基序保留表示），这是一种拓扑感知的分子语言，旨在连接片段级表示学习与精确的结构编辑。STAMP通过分别编码基序身份、连接位点及树拓扑结构，使得分子片段在不同上下文中具有可重用性。实验表明，STAMP在分子编辑、优化及转换任务中表现优异，在多个基准测试中超越了传统的SMILES编码方法，为可执行的分子设计提供了新的语言框架。
